newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest runoff to hydropower projects rises.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest runoff to hydropower projects rises.

text.p: Spring runoff at hydroelectric power projects in the Pacific Northwest is back up to seasonal levels, sources at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Portland, Ore., said Wednesday.
"Temperatures have increased and flows are now closer to where we would expect them to be given the high snowpack," a reservoir control center operator at the federal agency said.
Cold weather earlier this month, particularly in mountainous areas, limited the amount of water available for hydropower generation.
The Corps spokesman noted flows into the Lower Granite dam on the Snake River are forecast at 180,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) this weekend, compared with lows of 80,000 cfs last week.

In its last forecast update, the Northwest River Forecast Center estimated January-July runoff at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River in Oregon at 141 percent of normal, the second highest rate since record-keeping began in 1929.
Runoff at some Snake River projects is forecast at more than 160 percent of normal levels.
